changes: The Muse spider in Bot details indicates thinking, work and pending user input. A successful turn plays a short animation in its own conversation. The avatar respects reduced-motion settings
NOTICE is the upstream repository's root NOTICE, copied beside the plugin so the packaged plugin carries its attribution

`config.agentPreset` names the product preset every Bot conversation is created on (own chat, group member Sessions, new parts); a group's relay Session stays on `standard`; a configured preset the host does not serve fails the creation

`cordis.patch.yml` is Muse's composition: one `bot` row with `agentPreset: short-drama-v2` (the lean prompt with craft skills; `short-drama` stays for existing Sessions) and `updateCheck: false`, the host settings shell off, and no upstream web-search row, so Muse's own search provider stays in effect; the desktop build also omits `web-search.js`, the `bin/` doctor and the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web` peer

The plain-session row is named "Muse 会话" and always exists (`ensureAgent` at team bootstrap, no first Session); its menu no longer offers removal, because removing the row archives every Session it holds

The row works in one workspace: unfolded it shows a workspace picker first (the pick is kept in `localStorage` under `ds-bot:agent-workspace`, else the workspace of its latest Session), nothing opens before a workspace is picked, new Sessions are made in that workspace, and only that workspace's Sessions are listed
The ordinary Sessions of the picked workspace join the row through the `agent-sync` endpoint (`syncAgentSessions`), which skips every Session a Bot, a group or the row already owns
`client.js` is rebuilt from `src/client` by the Muse plugin build; the committed copy is upstream's and does not contain the changes above

Settings and the account menu no longer offer "Classic Agent mode"; Settings still offers the way back when a window is already in that mode, and the hint shown when the Bot team fails to start still offers the classic view

When a conversation moves on to a fresh part, `moveOn` emits the host event `task-skill/carry` before the handoff package, so the task skills in effect stay in effect in the fresh part; `canMakeRoom` counts the skill-invocation messages of the current part as carried again, so a part that holds little besides its skills is not replaced over and over

Brand: the interface says "Muse". `t()` and `hostText()` replace "DS Bot", "DeepSeek Harness" and the word "DSH" in shown text after translation; the sidebar name, the About name, the notification title and one refusal line are literals changed in place. Host-side text is changed at its source (see the entry on host-side text)

The Muse spider (`src/client/muse-spider.js`, the artwork also shipped in `packages/client/ui-session-coordinator`) is the `muse-spider` character and `MAIN_LOOK`, so the first Main Bot and every brand mark use it; the composition names the first Main Bot "Muse" with the role "主理人"; the "Muse 会话" row and its palette entry use the chats icon instead of the DeepSeek whale

About no longer asks for a GitHub star, requests the star count or links to the upstream repository; Feedback keeps the diagnostics copy, links to Muse's own suggestion box (the address the account plugin publishes as `__MUSE_FEEDBACK_CONFIG__.feedbackUrl`) and no longer opens an issue in the upstream repository; Settings has no Phone page, because pairing needs the upstream phone app
With update checks off, About shows no version under the name, no Updates section and no release-notes link; Feedback drops the "What happened?" field, which only fed the upstream issue
An artwork character with `solidEyes` (the Muse spider) keeps its body unmasked and draws dark eyes with a highlight on top, with a thinner happy-eye arc

The command shield no longer re-registers its shadows on a context that is already gone: an agent's scope unwinds before `agent/disposed`, lifting the shadows announces `commands/change`, and every quit or agent unload used to log one "could not be shadowed … inactive context" warning per command
The command shield's refusal and menu texts are Chinese and no longer say "DSH"; the host shows them as written

Trailing spaces and extra blank lines at the end of `client.js`, `src/client/connector-marks.js` and eleven test files are removed so the repository whitespace check passes; the code is otherwise unchanged

Sidebar header shows the bare Muse spider (`src/client/muse-brand.js`, a mask painted in the text color, black on light and white on dark) beside the name; the foot replaces the gear and the Plugins button with the user's capsule (avatar and Muse account name, opening the account menu), a "Skills/MCP" button (the Capabilities page) and a round asset-library button (the `character-library` page, where registered)

The details drawer has tabs for Details, Browser, Side chat, Terminal, Files, Jingliu and the asset library. The Jingliu tab shows the local project for the current conversation or the hosted workbench. Bot details show current, running and earlier sessions, a New session action, a language-model line and the Background controls

Verified dsh-im Feishu connections preserve Muse Bot chat bindings, stored display names and original reply routes. Settings → IM combines Bot execution settings with the selected account's Feishu settings. Progress cards and optional voice replies use the verified account
Muse's own interface strings are translated in the Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French and German dictionaries, as upstream's locale test requires; that test's allowed English names include "Muse"

Settings: an Account page comes first (`src/client/account-page.js`): the user's avatar (another character, or an uploaded picture, saved as the team preference `you`, which the host validates), the Muse account's user name and ID and, following Feishu, the department and Feishu name, with the Muse account section itself below; the list then reads General, Models, Local agents, Connectors, IM, Computer use, Secrets, Usage, a rule, the team pages (Bots, Bot models, Group chats, Skills/MCP, Browser, Scheduled tasks), DSH's sections without the Muse account one, and Feedback and About. The sidebar's user capsule opens the Account page

The details drawer renders two slots, `bot.drawer.jingliu` and `bot.drawer.assets` (declared as children of the overlay entry, owner `{ sessionId }` = the Bot's current conversation): where a plugin fills one, its tab shows that view inside the drawer instead of opening a page

The drawer slots also get `quote(text)` and `compose(text)` for the Bot's conversation: `actions.quote(sessionId, text, { plain: true })` puts the text into the message box as written instead of as a quote; the sidebar's asset button opens the current Bot's drawer on its asset tab where `bot.drawer.assets` is filled

Host-side text that reaches the model, IM users or sign-in pages names Muse instead of DS Bot: Bot persona and handoff/checkpoint requests, memory prompts, group notices and their sender, tool descriptions and results, errors, IM replies, connector sign-in pages, the dynamic-registration client name, the IMAP ID, and the name of workspaces the Bot creates. Code comments, developer logs and the diagnostics row naming the upstream plugin version keep DS Bot

`config.oauthClientDocument` (an https:// address, checked at load) names the client ID metadata document new connector sign-ins use; unset keeps upstream's `https://dsbot.app/oauth/client.json`. A connector signed in through a document keeps refreshing with that document, and a stored document client is not reused for a new sign-in once another document is configured

Declined skill proposals stay scoped to their Bot (restored from the earlier Muse Bot): each decline records the Bot it was proposed to, and a Bot's skill review lists only its own declines, so a private Bot's declines never reach another Bot's model request; ownerless records saved before stay on disk and enter no request

PowerPoint inventory and layout apply nested group coordinates from the nearest group to its ancestors (restored from the earlier Muse Bot), in `src/office/pptx.js` and the committed `office.js` bundle

Tests follow Muse behavior: the always-present Muse 会话 row, the Chinese command-shield texts, the Muse spider as the first Main Bot, Muse names, the suggestion box instead of GitHub issues, and no classic Agent mode switch. The committed-bundle checks for `client.js` and `link.js` and the phone relay tests are skipped, because Muse bundles `src/client` at build time and does not vendor upstream's `link` sources

Sidebar foot: the Skills/MCP button is gone (the Capabilities page stays in Settings); the asset-library button shows pressed while the drawer is on the library and a second press returns the drawer to its details (`noteDrawerTab` records the tab the open drawer shows)

Details drawer: a group's drawer has no tabs; the Bot details no longer list Connectors (they stay in Settings); while a Jingliu project tab shows, the panel opens at least 900 px wide as far as the window allows; the slots' owner props carry `quote` and `compose`

A Main Bot's own chat shows team activity in a capsule above the message box (`TeamDock` in `member-status.js`). The capsule expands upward from its bottom edge, replacing the summary with rows for each Bot. Pending approvals and single-choice questions can be answered in place, and working rows show elapsed time and open the Bot's chat

Settings → Account: seven characters to pick from, and the Follows Feishu block always shows with a lock (department, job title, manager, Feishu account; a value Feishu sync does not provide shows a dash)
A message handed to another Bot reads 已交给 in Chinese

A Bot's drawer keeps its tab row under the Bot's name (`drawerTabs` in `side-model.js`): Details, Browser, Side chat, Terminal, Files, Jingliu, Asset library and Computer, each shown only where it can be used, with the tab's content below the row. The panel's strip holds only what was opened: the Bot's own tab, browser pages, side chats and Jingliu projects, and it appears once one of those exists. The Bot's avatar, name and settings gear hide only while a Jingliu project tab shows. The sidebar has no separate Jingliu entry (`canOpenJingliu` / `openJingliu` are gone)

A Jingliu project opens as a strip tab of its own (`openJingliuProject` / `closeJingliuProject`, kept per panel in the UI state for the run), so several can be open; the Jingliu slot gets `project` (null on the list tab) and `openProject`

The Files tab shows the conversation's working folder as a tree inside the panel (`src/client/files-tree.js`, host endpoint `files-list` → `rt.workFiles`): one level at a time, folders first, hidden entries left out, links not followed, nothing outside the working folder; a file row puts its path into the message box
A message's reaction, reply and more buttons stay in view under it beside its time (`bt-afoot`); earlier bubbles of the same message keep theirs on hover

A group's relay Session runs on the product preset where the host keeps `standard` for existing Sessions only (`presets.resolveForCreation`); creating a group failed on Muse's desktop with "Agent preset is only available for existing sessions: standard"

Terminals open inside the Bot's panel where a plugin fills the `bot.drawer.terminal` slot (DSH's terminal tab plugin does): the Terminal tool beside the gear lists the conversation's terminals as cards under the Bot's name (`src/client/terminal-cards.js`, the Host's terminal list through `webTerminals.watch`), a card or New terminal opens the terminal in a strip tab of its own (`openTerminalTab` / `closeTerminalTab`, tab key `terminal:<key>`, kept per panel in the UI state for the run) and the Bot's own strip tab goes back to the list. The panel reports its open tabs to `webTerminals.retainTabs` under the layout name `bot-panel`, closing a tab ends its terminal, and an open terminal takes the browser's panel widths. Without the slot the Terminal tab still hands off to DSH's right column

The drawer's top has an export button again, left of Close: it downloads the conversation's Session log through DSH's `sessionLogDownload` service (the ZIP of the Session, its sub-sessions and attachments) instead of copying the conversation as Markdown; it shows only where that service runs

Drawer tabs (`side-model.js` `drawerTabs`/`drawerTools`, `details-drawer.js`): the row under a Bot's name is 详情 · 浏览器 · 剧本 · 镜流 · 资产库 · 数据 in equal tabs; Side chat, Terminal and Files are round tools beside the gear. The 数据 tab is the `bot.drawer.data` slot and the 剧本 tab the `bot.drawer.scripts` slot. An open Jingliu project, finalized script or data platform is a strip tab (`jingliu:<id>`, `script:<id>`, `data:<id>`; `ui.jingliuTabs`/`scriptTabs`/`dataTabs` through the shared `openListTab`/`closeListTab` in `team-actions.js`) that takes the drawer and widens the panel like the Jingliu workbench (`overlays.js`)

On a macOS window the shell's title-row sidebar opener (`data-sidebar-opener`) is the column's only switch: `sidebar.js` catches its click like the shortcut and `styles.js` hides the rail's round `bt-side-collapse` and the hidden column's `bt-title-toggle` while it is shown; the wide column covers the opener and keeps its own switch

The drawer's three tools share one capsule beside the gear with classes of its own (`bt-dtools`, `bt-dtool`): `.bt-tools` and `.bt-tool` are the message tools', which stay hidden until a message is hovered. The row under the Bot's name is one track with the tab in view as a raised pill (`.bt-tabs-many`)

A group's relay step asks the tool registry whether the Session's Agent can call `group_relay` when the request does not list it (`groups.js`): Muse's desktop shows tools to the model on demand, so the tool is callable but never listed for a Session that consults no model, and group messages got the line "its relay tool is not available" instead of reaching the Bots. A request that lists `run_code` keeps the PTC path

A group's drawer has the library tabs too (`drawerTabs` with `room`): 详情 · 剧本 · 镜流 · 资产库 · 数据, each where a plugin fills its slot; what a tab hands over goes to the group's message box. The browser, the computer and the tools stay a Bot's own. A group's panel shows the strip once a script, project or platform is open, with the group in the place of the Bot's own tab and no `···` menu

Computer is the fourth tool in the capsule beside the gear (`drawerTools` with `computer`), shown where the desktop offers computer use; it is no longer a row tab, so a Bot's row is 详情 · 浏览器 · 剧本 · 镜流 · 资产库 · 数据. Pressing it shows the computer view under the Bot's name, as the row tab did

Settings → Connectors lists Jubian (剧变), a production channel rather than an MCP server, first among the recommended tiles and only where the Jubian plugin registers its `jubian` settings section: the tile opens that section (the plugin's own token form) inside the page, shows connected once the Host holds a token (`actions.jubianStatus` reads `remote.jubianToken.describe()`), and the section is no longer a page of its own in the settings navigation

IM chat Bots (`im/index.js`, `roster.js` `greet: false`, `tools.js` `im_send`): a chat app chat with no binding of its own gets a Bot of its own the first time it writes, named after the chat, filed in the platform's sidebar section (飞书, …) and made without a greeting turn: every group and every private chat, the connection owner's included; an owner's private chat that used the connection's Bot without a binding gets its own on its next message, and a chat bound by hand keeps its binding. A chat whose Bot was deleted gets a new one; `chatBots: false` on a connection leaves chats to bindings made by hand and private chats to the connection's Bot. `/new` starts a fresh part of the chat's Bot. `im_send` lets a Bot write to its own chats unprompted, for results, reports and alerts; the connection's Bot also reaches the owner's private chat (recorded by the person id each private chat keeps), whose replies go to that chat's Bot

The data station's 储备 changes wake the supervising Bot (`station-events.js`): with `MUSE_STATION_EVENTS_SECRET_FILE` (or config `stationEventsSecretFile`) naming a private secret file, the route `POST /api/muse/station-events` verifies the station's HMAC-SHA256 signature over timestamp and body (5-minute window), and turns each batch of job changes into one message in the chat of the Bot named by `MUSE_STATION_EVENTS_BOT` (or config `stationEventsBot`), else the first main Bot (`rt.sendUser`, request id `station:<deliveryId>`); a repeated delivery id is acknowledged without a second message, and without that Bot or a secret the station is told to retry (503)

The Bot or group avatar in Details shows thought bubbles while it owns background work. Each bubble expands over the details view with its status and actions, and the overflow bubble expands to show the task list. Stop targets an individual job, terminal or open turn. Pause and Resume control future scheduled deliveries. Bot and group settings offer an entry for adding scheduled tasks

IM names and access (`im/index.js`, `im/platforms/feishu.js`, `im-page.js`, `account-page.js`): the Feishu adapter reads each chat's name and its members' names (`im:chat:readonly`, cached ten minutes, ids stand in when it cannot) and still hands messages on in arrival order. A chat Bot is named after the group, or after the person in a private chat; a Bot that still carries an id takes the real name once it can be read, and a Bot renamed by hand keeps its name. Settings → IM gains the old IM plugin's access settings per connection: for private chats and for groups, who can talk (approved people or everyone) and who can use commands and approvals (`/stop`, `/new`, approval answers and buttons: everyone who can talk, or only the owner), with a per-person Commands switch (`im-person`) and the A Bot for each chat switch. The Account page reads the Feishu name from the profile and the departments from the account-level organization, so a relay sign-in shows them, each as its path below the enterprise root

Account page job title and manager (`account-page.js`): 职位 and 上级 show the Feishu job title and direct manager's name that the account gateway's organization sync now sends with the account-level organization (`jobTitle`, `managerName`); either stays a dash when Feishu gives none or the application may not read it

Sidebar foot: a round quota button right of the user's capsule in the open column and below it on the rail (`src/client/quota.js`) shows the Muse user's Jingliu credit (积分, 1 积分 = 1 元) read through the `jingliuConnection` Remote that ui-jingliu mounts (`balance`, injected with 'remote'), on mount, every minute (five while the window is hidden), when the window shows again (or a minute after a read that started less than 15 s before), after a Muse sign-in change or a reconnect, and when its popover opens; it renders only once a read has answered that the Host serves that namespace, and a sign-in change or a reconnect never brings it back where the Host does not; a failed read shows an unknown state instead of a figure, the button adds a red dot only when Jingliu enforces a depleted balance, the button's accessible name carries the figure, and the popover above it takes focus and shows what is left (or 不限额), 已用 and 冻结中, the line 额度已用完，生成已停下，请找组长划拨。 when used up, and a row that opens Settings → 余额与费用

Settings → 余额与费用 reads the signed-in user’s Jingliu balance and recent ledger entries through the same connection. It shows signed balance changes and clears in-flight results when the login changes. Jubian shows connection status and Muse model usage links to the token report

Sidebar: every Main Bot is a tile at the top of the open column, side by side in `mainBotIds` order (`mainBotsOf` in `sources.js`, `.bt-tiles` in `styles.js`): three fit the narrowest column, more wrap to the next line, a long name or label is cut with an ellipsis, and one Main Bot looks as it did. On the rail they are avatar rows above the rule. A Main Bot is no longer listed below, and what asked whether a Bot is the tile now answers for every Main Bot: no pin, no drag into a section, no section entries in its menu or in a section's add list, no Sidebar card in its settings (`sidebar.js`, `context-menu.js`, `bot-settings.js`); removing the role returns it to the list. `mainBotId`, the first one, stays where the app lands and where the start window's hand-off glides. A Bot linked to a chat app wears that app's mark on its avatar in the sidebar, tile and row (`imLinksOf` in `sources.js`, `im` on `BotAvatar` and `imLabel` in `mark.js`, `.bt-badge-im`): the Bot of an enabled IM connection and the Bot each of its chats is bound to, read from the roster's `im` view. Feishu / Lark takes precedence on a Bot linked to several chat apps, and its mark is drawn in `connector-marks.js`; Telegram, WeChat, QQ, Discord and Slack reuse theirs; DingTalk and WeCom have no mark and show none. The mark sits on the avatar's right edge above the state, Main and admin badge, and the row's accessible name says "Linked to {name}" in every locale

IM reply origin (`im/index.js` `isModelContext`): a user-role message in a chat's turn is model context, and neither claims nor withdraws the chat, when its source declares a form other than `relay` or is one of the form-less context producers `compact-checkpoint`, `cordis-host-runner`, `output-continuation`, `ptc-mode`, `working-directory`, `screenplay-project-read` and `jubian-video-selection`. A Feishu turn with memory snapshots or a compaction checkpoint before its message, or notices and skill or agent instructions after it, answers in Feishu; peer Bot and agent relays, `user-approval`, Web, phone and scheduled messages withdraw it. A turn that a notice (a settled sub-agent, a finished job, a Jubian result) wakes by itself answers no chat: a Bot's turn start clears the origin, and in a group's own Session the notice, as the turn's first message, settles the deferred reset

Company members (Muse Central, `central-members.js` on Host and client): with `MUSE_CENTRAL_MEMBERS=1`, a fixed HTTPS `MUSE_BASE_URL` and an exact `MUSE_CENTRAL_ORIGIN` (plus an optional exact `http://127.0.0.1` `MUSE_CENTRAL_LOOPBACK_ORIGIN`), the Host registers `POST /api/bot/central-members` and puts `centralMembers` (the account origin) into the roster. The route accepts only those Web origins, refuses read-only Hosts, and uses the signed-in Muse administrator's `__Host-muse` cookie from `muse-account/session.json`, which stays on the Host: `list` reads `/api/admin/accounts` and returns id, name, revision, disabled, admin, own and groups only; `groups` and `disabled` check the member's revision and the session again, then post `/admin/groups` or `/admin/disable` and succeed only on the gateway's `303 /admin`. The administrator cannot disable their own account. The wide sidebar shows a collapsed Company members section after the Bot list (`sidebar.js`, `.bt-central*`), with search, 24 rows per page, a menu for details, groups and disable or enable, and a dialog per action; its 22 strings are translated in every locale

The Muse spider is a vector drawing that takes the Bot's color (`src/client/muse-spider.js`, generated by `dev/spider.mjs`): the approved artwork (`packages/client/ui-muse-market/src/client/assets/muse-purple-spider.png`, whose square is the character's 100-unit box) is traced into its outline, nested translucent shade steps and one translucent light layer, whose colors and opacities are measured so that on the artwork's own purple they give the artwork's tones. The violet ink shows that purple in both themes (`inks` on the shape, read by `characterMarkup`), any other color or gradient fills the same drawing, the eyes stay the artwork's and are drawn on top, the picker's selection ring and the @mention mark follow the traced outline, and an unpainted box of the former picture keeps the mark's motion as it was. The 200×133 bitmap body is gone from the bundle. `dev/trace.mjs` holds the contour tracing and path writing that `dev/characters.mjs` had, now shared with the spider tracer; the 20 generated characters are unchanged; `scripts/style-debt.mjs` counts `muse-spider.js` among the generated palettes

Settings → IM chats list (`im-page.js` `TargetMenu` `fallback`): every chat row, group or private, has the same picker of Bots and group chats. A private chat with no target of its own shows the connection's Bot with the muted mark Follows “Talks to” (跟随对话对象), and the same entry heads its menu: choosing it clears the chat's binding (`im-chat` with `target: null`), choosing a Bot or a group chat binds the chat. A group's first entry stays Not bound

IM chats set to no target by hand (`im/index.js` `im-chat`, `wantsOwnBot`): choosing 跟随对话对象 (Follows “Talks to”) for a private chat or 未绑定 (Not bound) for a group in Settings → IM sends `target: null`, which records `manual: true` on the chat and drops its `botName`; chat Bots then leave the chat alone, so a private chat keeps answering through the connection's Bot and a group stays unbound. Binding the chat to a Bot or a group chat clears `manual`. A chat without the field, or a build that ignores it, behaves as before: an unbound chat gets a Bot of its own when it next writes

The Bot view keeps no rail of the shell's collapsed sidebar on any platform (`index.js` shell group, `ctx.layout.hideSidebarRail()` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-layout`): on the web the collapsed sidebar kept its 56px rail, with the floating expand switch over it and the settings gear at its foot, whenever the right column was open or the window was narrower than 1024px. The shell now gives that column no track, as the desktop apps already did, at every width. The `styles.js` grid override that zeroed the track only for a wide window with the right column closed is gone, and `frame-watch.js` counts the collapsed track as empty until it is measured

Update checks are off unless the config sets `updateCheck: true` (`update.js` `updateChecksOn`, also read by `dsh-update.js`): a profile whose `bot` entry replaces the plugin's whole config dropped `updateCheck: false`, and the upstream default then looked up ds-bot on npm, offered upstream releases and could remove and reinstall the bundle. Without the field no check is scheduled, `update-check` asks no registry, neither the DS Bot reinstall nor the DSH `npm install -g` is offered, the sidebar shows no update button, and Settings → About shows no Updates section. `updateCheck: true` restores the checks as they were; `cordis.patch.yml` keeps `updateCheck: false`

The team capsule opens into one bubble in one motion (`TeamDock` in `member-status.js`, driven by `src/client/team-dock-motion.js`): a single SPRING_SHAPE value takes the same surface from the capsule to the bubble (width, height and corner radius together, anchored at the bottom centre), and everything that travels is placed from that value, so a second press mid-way turns round from where it stands: each avatar flies from its seat in the capsule to the start of its Bot's row and back, the capsule's words and the first row's words keep one place between the two (`data-lead`, when nobody is waiting), the other rows clear in 35 ms apart, the count leaves as the second row arrives and the chevron turns with the surface. The bubble is always `min(100%, 360px)` wide, so rows and elapsed times do not re-wrap while it grows. A Bot that starts or finishes adds or removes its avatar and its row with an entrance and an exit (`withLeaving` keeps what left for one SPRING_SHAPE), the capsule's width follows its summary on the same spring, and the capsule itself rises in and sinks out with the first and the last Bot. With `data-bt-effects` `reduced` or `off`, or the system's reduced-motion setting, nothing travels or blurs and nothing lingers: the change is at once, with at most a plain fade. Keyboard and screen-reader behaviour is unchanged

Feishu message types (`im/platforms/feishu.js`, `im/platforms/feishu-dsh-im.js`, `im/index.js`): a rich-text `post` flattens to its title and paragraphs (a link keeps its text and address, a mention its name, the bot's own mention is dropped) and its pictures and videos are downloaded; `file` and `media` messages are downloaded through the message resource endpoint, up to 100 MiB, and handed on as files; a voice message is turned into text by dsh-im where its speech service is set up and handed on as `audio.opus` elsewhere (the native adapter always hands it on as a file). On the dsh-im connection the rich consumer forwards every message type and DS Bot downloads only once a message is admitted; the native adapter fetches nothing for a group message that does not mention the bot. A message with nothing readable (a sticker, a forwarded bundle, a share card, an empty post) is handed on with `unsupported: <message_type>`: the core answers a person who may talk, where the bot was spoken to, with one line (`unreadable`, in all eight languages) and logs the platform, chat kind and type. Upstream read only plain text and a single image and dropped everything else without a reply

Feishu groups register themselves (`im/index.js`, `im/platforms/feishu.js`, `im/platforms/feishu-dsh-im.js`): the Feishu handles, native and dsh-im, gain `chats()`, which lists the groups the bot is in (`GET /open-apis/im/v1/chats`, ten pages of 100, with the app credentials DS Bot holds), and the native adapter reports `im.chat.member.bot.added_v1` through a new optional `onChat` handler (dsh-im does not forward that event, so a dsh-im connection picks a new group up at its next listing). The core registers every listed group not yet known as a chat with a Bot of its own, through the same path a first message takes, when the connection turns ready, every ten minutes while it stays ready and on `onChat`; Bots are made one after another, a known chat only follows its name (so a deleted chat Bot is not made again until the chat writes), `chatBots: false` records the chat without a Bot, and a list that cannot be read is logged once per connect. Leaving a group is not followed. Platforms without `chats()` are unchanged

`im_send` and `im_history` (`im/index.js`, `tools.js`): the Bot a connection belongs to reaches every chat registered on that connection, by title or key, not only the chats whose messages come to it; other Bots keep their own chats. Listed chats go by title, with the key where a title is missing or shared. What is sent is not passed to the chat's own Bot

Feishu replies keep their formatting (`im/feishu-markdown.js`, `im/platforms/feishu.js`, `im/platforms/feishu-dsh-im.js`, NOTICE): a reply that uses Markdown goes out as schema 2.0 cards with one `markdown` element instead of a text message; a plain reply stays text. On a dsh-im connection with the rich consumer the cards answer the source message (in its topic) through DS Bot's Feishu REST access, and plain replies and any chunk Feishu will not take as a card still go through dsh-im's checked reply. Ported from the retained dsh-im source (`feishu-cards.mjs`, `bridge.mjs`, MIT, recorded in NOTICE): the 24,000-byte budget of one card's content, the five-table limit of one card with its GFM table detection and the cut where a table begins, and plain text when the card is refused (a 4xx other than 401 and 403). dsh-im rewrites no Markdown; added here: a picture given by address becomes a link and one given by a local path its caption, because a card draws pictures only from Feishu image keys, and a code fence cut by chunking is closed and opened again

dsh-im for every channel (`im/platforms/dsh-im.js`, `im/index.js`, `im-page.js`, `settings.js`, `tools.js` `im_history`, `shared/im-platforms.js`): one adapter takes any dsh-im account through dsh-im's channel-neutral external consumer; connections link through the `dshIm` option (the older `feishuDshIm` still works) or Settings → IM, which lists unlinked dsh-im accounts with a Bot picker, and a link pins the account fingerprint. Replies go back to the message that asked; a chat's delivery route is saved so it can be written to first; attachments load only for admitted messages; `im_history` reads a chat back through dsh-im

Animated avatars, on by default (`animated-avatar.js`, `avatar-definitions.js`, `dev/avatar-definitions.mjs`): Settings → Bots → Animation has one switch, Animated avatars (`animatedAvatars` in the team preferences, stored only when off, like `enterToSend`: no key is on, `false` is off, and a `true` stored while off was the default is on and goes with the next on; a team that turned it on and off again while off was the default has no key and sees it on). While it is off every avatar is the drawn mark, no canvas is mounted, the finished-run hold stays 1.8 s and `copyOf` in `mark-flight.js` is the clone with its own ids that the panel made before. While it is on, open-bot-avatar 0.3.1 (MIT, pinned in `devDependencies` and in the plugin build toolchain, bundled into the Client, named in NOTICE, its version and license text in the built package's `BUNDLED_LICENSES.md`) draws the seven default characters (star, moon, gumdrop, peanut, bunny, kitty, acorn) from definitions built from `CHARACTERS`: the body's outline scaled to the package's 8..92 box, and a level eye pair as tall and as far apart as the character's capsules, moved up to 6.5 units toward the middle on the five characters drawn turned to the right, where the package needs room to turn the eyes. It shows in two places only, the Main Bot tiles of the open sidebar (the first four move, later ones are one still picture) and the avatar of a Bot's details page, in the box of the drawn mark and under the same badges (`animated` on `BotAvatar`); a Bot with a picture, the Muse spider (`animatedDefinition` refuses it by name, so the vector spider of `muse-spider.js` and its `SpiderDetail` motion stay as they are) and every other character keep the drawn mark, as do rows, groups and chat. A Bot's state maps to the package's six (`alert` to `blocked`), its color to the ink's hex for the theme's mode (`inkHex` in `inks.js`; the gradient takes its text ink), the eyes to the surface behind, Interface motion to reduced motion or one still picture, and the Bot's name to the accessible label; the pointer on an avatar makes it happy and the details avatar follows the pointer, unless Bot animation is quiet; a finished run holds the package's celebration for 3.9 s. A copy of the details avatar that flies to the panel's strip is painted from its canvas (`copyOf` paints only the canvas of an animated avatar)
